stories.title: Winbond announces low-power CUBE-Lite memory for edge AI, targeting 2027 production
stories.summary:
Winbond announced CUBE-Lite on November 4, a semi-custom memory design aimed at AI image processors, wearables, microcontrollers and other embedded AI systems.[1] The company reports up to 8 GB/s bandwidth at approximately 70 mW and roughly 20 ns access latency; these are vendor engineering figures, not independent device-level benchmarks.[1] Winbond also says its simplified interface can reduce controller power compared with an LPDDR4x implementation, but that does not establish the power savings of a complete product.[1] CUBE-Lite is still undergoing product validation, with mass production targeted for the first half of 2027, so it is not a generally shipping component today.[1] For edge-AI builders, the announcement highlights memory bandwidth and power as design constraints worth measuring alongside model accuracy. A practical services niche is hardware-selection and power-budget evaluation for private, on-device vision systems.

Sources:
[1] https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/winbond-introduces-cube-lite-edge-140000391.html

stories.title: Parloa and Deloitte Canada pair customer-service AI with integration and managed services
stories.summary:
Parloa announced an alliance and reseller agreement with Deloitte Canada on November 4 to bring its AI Agent Management Platform to Canadian customer-service operations.[3][5] The delivery scope includes contact-centre strategy, agent design, enterprise-system integration, governance and change management, with ongoing optimization and managed services extending beyond platform resale.[3] This is a Canada-specific expansion of an existing relationship, not the first partnership between the companies.[3] Unite.AI also describes Parloa Zones as a regional processing boundary for conversations, transcripts, logs and analytics, making data-residency verification part of implementation work.[3] The sources do not disclose engagement prices, named customer deployments under this agreement or independently measured savings.[3][5] For an agency, the useful model is a bounded customer-service workflow with explicit human escalation, integration acceptance tests and a recurring monitoring agreement rather than an unqualified promise to replace the contact centre.

Sources:
[3] https://unite.ai/parloa-forms-deloitte-canada-alliance-for-ai-customer-service
[5] https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/parloa-expands-north-american-agentic-cx-footprint-through-alliance-with-deloitte-canada-302928105.html
